All 16 colours share one layout (64-grid alpha pattern identical); red_n.png = Java-layout normal map (unused by the engine).

  MARKER ENTITY pw:marker — properties pw:fam int 0..3 (zone/station/port/datum), pw:icon int 0..63 (FROZEN append-only table: zones 0-11 in precedence order, stations 12-29 alphabetical, ports 30-33, datum 34), pw:n int 0..63 (zone corner = ring*16+idx exactly as the block states; station/port index 0..7), pw:vis bool.   NUMBERING: identical to v0.1.9 (zone: per player, kind change = new ring, n 0..63, civ:zone close/status; station/port: per player+role 0..7, civ:station reset) + the open zone ring survives a reload (player dynamic property).

  MIGRATE: civ:markers migrate [r] converts pw:zone_/station_/port_/datum BLOCKS within r (default 32, y +-16) into entities with the same kind/number; blocks stay registered so old saves load. civ:markers list [r] prints every marker by kind/number; civ:markers check [r] lists NON-marker entities in range (pre-save: saves now need Include Entities ON).
  HATCH LID pw:hatch_lid (item pw:hatch_lid, use it on the TOP ladder of an opening): entity at the ladder cell centre, y+0.8125, collision box 1.0 x 0.1875 (top flush with the floor above); CLOSED = minecraft:is_collidable (happy-ghast adult_immobile pattern: is_collidable + body_rotation_blocked + knockback 1, not pushable); OPEN = no is_collidable, leaf standing against the HINGE side inside the cell; tap = pw:toggle (first_valid on bool_property pw:open), either side (vanilla trapdoor semantics, not the manhole HATCH LAW); hinge side = the side the ladder FACES (ladder facing_direction 2/3/4/5 = N/S/W/E per mojang-blocks.json) = opposite the ladder; hit = remove (item back in survival); breaking the ladder removes the lid. Texture = RP-03 trapdoor.png (Patrix, 128², cut-outs) copied into Markers RP.

Evidence: (W) his 09:57 trader-llama shot (neck hanging below the body only under the verified law) + our witness-accepted cow (its body z sits at the Patrix ANIMATED rest value, reproduced only under the verified variable semantics); (D) Blockbench 4.12.4 codecs optifine_jem.js + bedrock.js (Euler order 'ZYX'; JEM->BB: origin=-translate, boxes as-is, rotate as-is; BB->Bedrock: x mirrored, rotation (-rx,-ry,+rz)); EMF source (EMFPartData/EMFBoxData: invertAxis negates translate/rotate components and mirrors boxes per axis; EMFModelOrRenderVariable: animated tx/ty/tz/rx/ry/rz SET the ModelPart fields = REPLACE semantics; EMFModelPartRoot: the custom part is attached as a CHILD of the vanilla part); the CEM Template Loader's animation player (tx=-x_BB, ty=24-y_BB (root)/-y_BB (submodel), tz=+z_BB; rx/ry/rz -> BB rotation (-,-,+), radians); (E) tools/r1_jem_vs_bedrock.py — the vanilla Java models in JEM form (CEM Template Models v5.0.3, 224 models) converted with CONV-1 reproduce Mojang's own Bedrock geometries: 240 cubes matched across 30 mobs (all non-restructured ones), 192 pivots exact, rotations 12/12 where vanilla keeps them in the file (pig, sheep, cow, llama chests [0,-90]->[0,90], turtle, panda, ravager horns, zombie_villager brim); every other sign triple fails (X or Y wrong).
  THE LAW (L-ROT-DIR, final form): (1) FILE FRAME: Bedrock geometry x is mirrored vs the world (file +x = the entity's LEFT; face names are world-based). (2) A bone rotation [rx,ry,rz] evaluated in file coordinates = Rz(-rz)·Ry(+ry)·Rx(-rx) (right-handed matrices, X applied first): +90 X puts the cube's local +Y at the FRONT (-z) and local +Z UP; +90 Y puts the front toward file -x (the entity's right); +rz tips the top toward file +x (the entity's left). (3) CONV-1 (JEM invertAxis xy -> Bedrock): pivot_B=(t.x,-t.y,-t.z); cube origin_B=(-(c.x+w),c.y,c.z); rotation_B=(-rx,-ry,+rz); uv* per face copies unchanged (north..down), textureOffset copies; sizeAdd->inflate; mirrorTexture u->mirror; submodels: pivot_BB = translate (absolute at depth 0, +parent pivot deeper), boxes relative to the submodel pivot. (4) CEM-RT (runtime): each JEM part is a child of the vanilla part; the vanilla part keeps its code pose (quadruped body +90 X etc.) unless the JEM assigns <part>.r*/t*; animated variables REPLACE the static values; rx in radians = Java angles = Bedrock degrees/57.3; tx/ty/tz = Java rotation-point coords (root: pivot_BB=(-tx,24-ty,tz)).
  SUPERSEDED (kept, tagged): §3.1 "positive X rotation tips the top toward +Z (backward)" -> toward -Z (front); §3.2 "[-rx, ry, -rz]" -> (-rx,-ry,+rz); §4.2 table inverted on X; §2.1 "+Y down, +Z forward" JEM frame -> the JEM(xy) frame is the WORLD frame (y up, -z front, +x = entity's right); §2.3 "negate Y" -> with invertAxis xy nothing is negated in y; x is mirrored for boxes only. Standard amended in place (supersession block), MOB-CONVERSION-RESEARCH-2026-09-27 carries the full derivation.

## D-C260 — [22:34 CT 09-27] P0 WIRING BUILDS SHIPPED: RP-07 1.4.12 · TestRunner 0.2.1 · BP-02 1.3.189 · RP-06/RP-08 1.4.7 (Abs0lum 21:56 "All go, but we're still waiting on the laptop")

**His three questions answered (in the reply):** (1) loader/version — one converter: Patrix is a resource pack whose mob models are OptiFine/EMF `.jem` files; Fabric/Forge/Quilt/NeoForge only pick the renderer mod, the bytes are identical; the MC VERSION matters only through the vanilla part tables the JEMs attach to → parameterise by version, never by loader. (2) cow/mooshroom "not married" (legs not touching, joints not staying connected) — mechanism WITH NUMBERS: `head` + `leg0–3` are ROOT bones; `animation.cow.pw.ambient` moves `body` alone: position y `0.5*sin(life_time*88)` + rotation x `2.0*sin(life_time*88)` about pivot [0,24,0] (14 cubes above the underside). Molang sin is in DEGREES (lesson L-MOLANG-DEG already in §8 — my earlier "≈14 Hz" ignored it: 88°/s = one breath per 4.1 s, 0.24 Hz). Neck (child of body) follows, head does not; legs do not → peak separation ≈ 0.5 + 9·sin 2° ≈ 0.8 cube at the body ends, slowly oscillating = exactly "not staying connected". Plus a constant −4° yaw on `leg3` (generator artefact). (3) tadpole — side-by-side sheet `r28-tadpole-vanilla-vs-patrix.png`; P8 correction: vanilla's tadpole is BROWN (not green as I wrote); the tell is the square vs tapered tail and 16× vs 128× texels; his shots show the taper → Patrix drawing; Patrix kept the vanilla silhouette, so "looks vanilla" is fair.

## D-C261 — [22:4x CT 09-27] TADPOLE CLOSED (Abs0lum 22:35 "You were right, the tadpole is Patrix quality") · MOB SIZE QUESTION (beetle/ant "too large" for hyper-realism) — proposal only
- r28 tadpole: CLOSED by his witness. Nothing to build.
- Measured from the shipped geometries (RP-07 1.4.12, sf_nba base): beetle 1.06 × 0.5 × **1.50** blocks · ant 0.62 × 0.69 × **1.00** · termite **1.44** long · snail 1.06 long · slug 1.06 · caterpillar 0.94 · dragonfly **1.49** wingspan · butterfly **2.06** wingspan · crab 0.69. Real animals: beetle 3–8 cm, ant ~1 cm, termite ~1 cm, snail 3–4 cm, slug 5–10 cm, caterpillar 3–6 cm, dragonfly 8–12 cm span, butterfly 6–10 cm span, crab 10–20 cm.
- Two levers: (1) RP `scripts.scale` on the client entity — visual only, per entity, no BP change; these entities ALREADY carry a scale expression (`q.is_riding ? 0.95 : 1`) so it is a one-number edit per mob; the hitbox stays the BP's. (2) BP `minecraft:scale` component in the entity definition — scales the model AND the collision box (the baby-zombie mechanism); the sf_nba behaviour side lives in PW-StripMine-BP (Realm-only). Recommendation: (2) for the Realm, since (1) leaves a 1.5-block hitbox around a 20-cm beetle. Texture density is unaffected either way (same texels, smaller on screen).
- Open for his pick: the exaggeration scheme — true scale (beetle 0.06 blk) is invisible on a phone; proposed FLOORED scheme: scale = max(real/current, floor) with the floor giving the smallest creatures ~0.2 blk (20 cm) → beetle ×0.13 (0.2 blk), ant ×0.2 (0.2), termite ×0.14, dragonfly ×0.13, butterfly ×0.1, snail ×0.19, caterpillar ×0.21, slug ×0.19, crab ×0.25 (0.17). Alternative 'half-real' floor 0.35 blk. Awaiting his answer; then a size audit of the whole roster (S/M) before any build.

## D-C268 — EQUINE FAMILY: WHAT PATRIX LOOKS LIKE vs OURS (his 18:36 "all the parts, oriented incorrectly, mispositioned, not connected naturally" — horse, mule/donkey + "another similar mob"; llamas/camels assembled right) — 19:2x CT 09-28
**Witness:** accepted as symptom truth (certainty language). My R2 read "married" was wrong in substance: I scored "touching" as "joined"; the head touches the neck at ONE CORNER, level, 12 px too far forward — not a natural joint.
**Reference (what it should look like):** web — Patrix 32x (Modrinth/CurseForge): mobs = "custom mob animation from FreshLX" (needs EMF/ETF/Fresh Animations); a Patrix showcase thumbnail (YouTube GaPoVjtQIE4) shows the horse's head angled DOWN-FORWARD continuing the neck line, two ears on top. Ground truth = the Patrix JEM + FreshLX rest pose, evaluated by cem_eval with the VANILLA per-frame seeds (neck ty 4 / tz -12 / rx 30°, body rx 0). Without seeds the horse evaluates REARING (var.rearing 0.5, because the JEM reads neck.ty < 4 → rearing) — cem_eval.rest_pose / bake_rest2 gained seeds= (backward compatible).
**Patrix rest (all five share the rig):** body → neck2 (pivot 0,18.7,-6.7, rx 31.5° forward) → { neck3 box, head2 (≈0° rel. = the head RIDES the neck, nose down 29°) → snout2 / ears (+8° back; donkey/mule rz ±15° splay) / mane3 }, mane2; tail2 13°.
**Ours (tools/equine_compare.py; the in-game prediction reproduces his 124030 horse, 124101 donkey, 124118 mule):**
- (1) POSITION: horse neck +7.1 px forward/+2.9 up; skull +11.9 fwd; muzzle +12.3 fwd/+4.5 up; ears +13.1 fwd; mane +7.2 fwd (1.2 px deep, half-buried → "no mane"); mule skull -7.0 px LOW + 13.2 fwd (head hangs off the neck's front middle); ears 1.0 px apart (overlap → "one ear"; Patrix 5 px apart / 3 px centre-to-centre, donkey/mule splayed ±15°). Neck 14 rows tall vs Patrix 12 (reads 2 extra texture rows).
- (2) ORIENTATION: `head` runs look_at with `relative_to: {rotation: entity}` (vanilla animation.common.look_at_target; the horse's own pw.headtrack also on head2) under a neck rotated 30° → the head's world orientation is reset to LEVEL (the neck's lean discarded), then head2/snout -10° each → donkey nose UP 10–20°. Patrix: nose DOWN 29°. Δpitch skull +29° (horse, zombie) / +39° (donkey, mule).
- (3) STRUCTURE: skeleton horse has NO neck (Patrix bone2 vertebrae ×2 absent); head floats level at chest height.
**Census (relative_to entity on a bone with a ROTATED ANCESTOR):** exactly horse (head, head2), donkey, mule, zombie horse — plus dolphin (body 0,0,180) and frog (body 0,45,0). Llama / trader llama / camel: no rotated ancestor → consistent with "assembled correctly".
**Proposed fix (awaiting GO):** Converter B for the equine family — geometry generated from the Patrix JEMs (CONV-1 + seeded rest bake; posture baked, leg stance static; our bone names kept so animations/RCs still bind; per-face UVs from the JEM) + a parent-relative look (FreshLX split: neck ry = clamp(yaw/2, ±20), neck rx += pitch/1.5, head ry = clamp(yaw/6, ±15)) replacing the relative_to look on these 5 entities. RP-07 1.4.15 (horse/donkey/mule) + RP-06 1.4.10 (zombie/skeleton horse); the ownership wave moves to RP-07 1.4.16 / RP-06 1.4.11.

## D-C273 — PHASE A census before the READY build (22:0x CT 09-28)
**Correction to my 21:18 preview (READY verdicts):** turtle + axolotl were NOT ready — the new models sat 12 px (turtle) and 22 px (axolotl) under the ground; the preview tiles had no ground reference so I did not see it. Dolphin sat 5-7 px behind the vanilla position.
**Mechanism (numbers):** OptiFine CEM attaches each JEM part model as a CHILD of the vanilla part: world = V + R_v·(p − D) (V/R_v = the vanilla part's runtime pivot/rotation, D = the JEM's declared pivot = −translate, p = the part content in Blockbench-absolute coordinates). Converter B's declared-pivot rule assumed V = D. FreshLX moves the vanilla part on purpose in: turtle body (ty 17, tz −1 → V (0,7,−1) vs D (0,0,−12)), axolotl body (t* = 0 → V (0,24,0) vs D (0,6,−1)), salmon body_front (tz 0 vs D −4). Dolphin body is not animated; its vanilla pivot (template) (0,0,−3) vs D (0,3,2). Check vs vanilla Bedrock geometry: exact rule → turtle shell y 3..9 / z −9..13 (vanilla shell 3..9 / −7..13); axolotl body2 pivot y 4 (vanilla body pivot y 4); dolphin z −13.8..25.3 (vanilla −13..25). Equines: V − D ≤ 0.4 px → the witnessed build is unchanged by the exact rule.
**Why not apply the exact rule everywhere:** FreshLX writes some vanilla translations in the Java PARENT frame (frog arms: ty −1.2 relative to the Java body → absolute formula gives +22 px; ravager legs). So V is honoured only per part, from an explicit table with the vanilla-placement evidence (PART_PIVOT in convb.py); every other part keeps the declared pivot (their V − D ≤ ~1.3 px).
**Frames:** our animations were written for entity-aligned parent frames. Bones whose rest parent frame is ≥ 45° off the entity frame get a frame bone that cancels it (rest pose unchanged): turtle head (under body 90°), wolf head/head2/mane/tail (under body 90°). Axolotl limbs under body2 15° are left (< 45°).
**Look:** relative_to looks → `animation.pw_convb.look` (additive on `head`, parent frame entity-aligned after the frame step), the witnessed equine approach (L-LOOK-REL).
**New gate lines:** placement vs vanilla (bbox centre / ground), animated-bone parent frame ≤ 45°, preview tiles carry a ground line.
**D-C273 SHIPPED (22:2x):** RP-07 v1.4.16 59,509,404 B md5 481aa0d5 (folder Szv3tbtz, PASS: server md5 == local, browser byte-exact). Gate verify_rp07_1416 90/90. Turtle rests in the neutral LAND pose (egg hidden, walk phase averaged). Sheets `_docs/convb/after_1416_1/2.png`. Plan: the ownership wave's RP-07 moves to 1.4.17.

## D-C278 — 03:0x–04:1x CT 09-29 — R4 witness intake (p3 run) + mechanisms
**Intake:** content log b34a6da6 (9,035 B, 200 lines, first line `[Scripting][warning]-[PW-TEST] setup cmd ok: fill ~-6 ~ ~-12 ~6 ~5 ~-2 air`) + 89 shots, ledger **89/89 VIEWED** (notes `_logs/r4_notes.md`).
**DIRECTIVE (his 03:03):** every test/witness item from now on is a TestRunner scriptevent.
**RULING (his 02:58):** Naturalist flying examples may go into our Realm pack; the focus is studying the method.
**New tool, bb_truth.py (the Blockbench/Bedrock face placement):** the display frame is the file frame with x mirrored. up/down per-face uv = [u+w, v+h] with size [-w, -h] (Blockbench bedrock.js parse/compile + cube.js UVToLocal). The old previews placed faces by name in the file frame and never showed the up/down turn.
- Validated against witness: the panda rump (023507) and the cold chicken (024212) match the truth render; the spider shot 022038 matches the truth render with the .tga.
**Mechanisms (P2):**
1. **UP/DOWN 180° (global converter bug).** jem_convert.face_uv copies JEM uvUp/uvDown [u1,v1,u2,v2] as uv [u1,v1] size [u2-u1, v2-v1]. Bedrock reads up/down turned 180° against the JEM/Blockbench display, so every up/down face of every JEM-derived geometry is rotated 180°. Explains the chicken feet (toes point back, 024212/024220), the frog feet (023118–023130), the panda rump upside down (the body is rotated 90°, so the rump is the box's top face) and the tropical fish bottom fins (3×3 plates; the fin art lands on the far edge, about 2 px off the belly, 023354). FIX in to_bedrock + flip the shipped JEM-derived geometries.
2. **SPIDER texture:** RP-07 ships textures/entity/spider/spider.png (Patrix 512×256) AND spider.tga (64×32 vanilla-like with opaque white regions). The game uses the .tga: the truth render with the .tga reproduces his white leg segments and abdomen strips. FIX: remove spider.tga. enderman.tga/.png is the same two-extension case and needs a check. LESSON CANDIDATE: inside one pack, the .tga shadows the .png of the same stem.
3. **SPIDER walk (n08):** the April spider.v1.8 walk drives leg1..8, which are mapped onto the Patrix HIP STUBS (leg_RF…, rest yaw ±20–70°). Its rotations were authored for the April leg axes: with a 70° rest yaw, the April roll becomes a twist, so the feet never lift, and position y 0.9–2.1 raises the hip only. FIX: port the Patrix knee/ankle walk (b/c/d rz + _2 ry swing from var.ls = modified_distance_moved/1.3).
4. **GUARDIAN spikes not smooth:** (a) the Bedrock-vanilla spike_shake = sin(t·2000°)/50 → ±0.23 px at 5.6 Hz on every spike, all the time; Java has NO in-water shake (GuardianModel: 1 + cos(age·1.5+i)·0.01 − ext). (b) query.is_moving is computed from motion each tick (Java isMoving is the AI flag), so it flickers for a hovering or held guardian: 25 %/tick retract steps against 6 %/tick extend = twitching. FIX: shake only out of water; a speed-based, smoothed moving signal with hysteresis. Both are Java-fidelity changes.
5. **RABBIT back feet 3 px up:** the JEM animates only head/ears; the feet/thighs/body/arms/tail hang on the Java parts (classic RabbitModel: feet (±3,17.5,3.7), haunch same + xRot −21° at rest, body (0,19,8) −20°, front legs (±3,17,−1) −11°, tail (0,20,7) −20°). The CEM template's rabbit is a different model (22.5° poses); ours used the DECLARED pivots → feet at y 3..4. FIX: RUNTIME_POSE rabbit (the guardian-spike mechanism). The body will tilt 20° like Java; preview first.
6. **DOLPHIN "parts?":** the JEM copies the vanilla fin pose (right_fin2.r* = right_fin.r*), but the CEM template has no fin rotation, so the seeds were 0 and the pectoral fins lie flat along the belly (022955–023005). Java DolphinModel fins: xRot 60°, zRot ∓120° (matching FreshLX's static −55/±120). FIX: seed patch.
7. **MOOSHROOM floating mushrooms:** vanilla Bedrock mooshroom.v2 geometry has NO mushroom cubes (body/udder/legs/head/horns/snout), so the game draws its own mushroom BLOCKS, like Java's layer, hung on the body/head bones. Our model's 6 planes never float (truth render); the floating tier in 023604 is blocky low-res 3D (block models), not our 512 art. HYPOTHESIS (untested): the engine places them in its vanilla frame relative to our body/head bones. TEST: A/B — red = bones renamed (pw_body/pw_head, no engine anchor), brown = current; TestRunner spawns both.
8. **RAVAGER `anim_nose`:** the ravager (RP-06) uses controller.animation.villager.nose_yaw, whose moving state plays `anim_nose`; the ravager defines `nose_yaw` only. FIX: alias (pillager too).
9. **CHICKEN wings/tail:** the truth render with the same camera matches his shot exactly (neck step, wing slab, drooping tail fan), so the game draws our model. The wings/tail are the JEM rest pose as converted. OPEN QUESTION to him: what should they look like?
10. **BEE 0.5×, AXOLOTL 0.8×** (his size asks). The bee is vanilla-sized now, so 0.5 = half of vanilla. The axolotl is 1.19× vanilla, so 0.8 ≈ 5 % under vanilla.
ASSUMPTION A-R4-1: the mooshroom engine blocks key on bone names body/head (to be settled by the A/B). ASSUMPTION A-R4-2: the rabbit's Java target is the classic RabbitModel (confirmed by feet-on-ground geometry only).

- MECHANISM (numbers + sources): Microsoft Learn "Exploring Custom Block Render Distance" (read today): opaque = far block, "rendered all the way up to the maximum render distance"; alpha_test (any other method) = near block, "up to *half* the maximum render distance". So shaped leaves visible past 70 blocks = his render distance is at least ~9 chunks (half >= 70) — his sight and the rule AGREE. BUT the scanner itself hands shaped leaves back to the cube at PW_FAR_OUTER = 72 blocks (far-reverter, main.js; shaped again inside PW_FAR_INNER 64), and it only CLASSIFIES leaves within PW_SCAN_RADIUS_XZ 25 of him — so unvisited forests beyond 25 blocks stay cubes (his "dark on first walkthrough"), and nothing beyond 72 is ever shaped whatever v0 looks like.
- So the lever is WHERE the handover happens and how far the scanner reaches, not only v0's look: (1) measure his half-distance on the PS5 (p14 probe: test blocks outside the scanner — shaped alpha_test, the far cube, and a C draft = the v4 shape with a filled opaque texture — side by side; he flies away, the bar shows the distance, he notes where the shaped one disappears); (2) move the handover out to just inside that distance; (3) widen the scanner reach (performance-tested: v1.2.35's lesson). ## D-C384 [12:27 CT 10-01] Flight v2 — three fixes after the first full batch
- G2 0.8 px on 30 spread-wing birds = MEASUREMENT artefact: posed_preview applies a position channel by shifting the
  subtree's file coordinates; wing_gap carried bind-local points through the posed affine WITHOUT that shift, so every
  hinge rotation counted the 1.5 px slide again (|d|·2·sin(θ/2) ≈ 0.8). Ablation: slide off → 0.19, hinges off → 0.
  Fix: local point + the bone's pivot delta. Tests: slide+hinge = 0; slid piece alone > 1.4; off-edge hinge > 0.5.
- Track-slide point: "centre of the north edge" put spread-wing pivots at MID-SPAN (eagle 13.8 px out) — the flap
  would rock the wing about its middle and pull the root off the body. New rule = centre of the wing's ROOT edge
  (end of the span nearest the shoulder). ASSUMPTION: for folded wings his "north edge" = the root edge; the two rules
  differ by 1–8 px on folded birds (root sits at the shoulder top, north-centre lower on the front edge) → shown to him
  for his eye before it is final.
- Cube-level rotations: 7 flying birds (WWA bird of paradise / roadrunner / shoebill / swan, WS desert owl / hornbill,
  YSav black eagle) have wing plates with cube rotation; every flight tool ignored it (frame, slide, stretch, hinge
  axis, gap + clip metrics) = the mechanism behind their big G3 / G2 numbers. New std_cube.py; hinges on those wings
  are an EXACT rotation about the shared edge (Rodrigues → Bedrock Z·Y·X euler in Molang; tests vs rot_matrix);
  stretch skipped on them (a bone scale would shear turned plates); hinge pivots moved onto the shared edge only for
  joints no other animation drives.
- F2 coverage: pw:turkey_wa + pw:kakapo_wwa were FLIGHT by id-set omission → FLUTTER; their step B redone (names only,

ROOT CAUSE of SHORT found in OUR tool: mers_derive.normal_156 writes z as z*255 instead of (z+1)/2*255 (flat pixels are identical, every tilted pixel decodes too short -> after the engine normalises, bumps are EXAGGERATED). Used for my phase 2/3/4/6 Patrix normals, the leaf builds and the mob tier-1 normals (RP-07). Not catastrophic (flat = right), but wrong. RP-03's dirt_n (B 173, older origin) is the same class.

## D-C432 SAND VV LUMPS (his 20:23 + 20:31) — intake 9/9 viewed

  Normal mean slope 7.4 deg, of which small-scale (<16 px) 5.9 deg, large-scale 2.8 deg -> the lumps are the small-scale part.

Mechanism candidate: a face whose column order (or u direction) is reversed relative to my static mapping -> tile pairs meet at their outer edges (e.g. 1 beside 4) = grain seam with no groove = his image. ## D-C487 [19:16 CT 10-02] ENGINE LAW MEASURED: minecraft:transformation rotation (BDS 1.26.52 rotprobe, job-only, never shipped)
- Probe _build/rotprobe-0.0.1: one octant collision/selection box (file origin [0,0,-8] size 8) under 12 rotations; downward getBlockFromRay at the 4 quarter-centres + a dropped item per cell. 13 records, 0 ERROR.
- RESULTS (world x east+, z south+, about the block centre y=8): (1) collision-box file +x lands at WORLD -x (same x-mirror as geometry). (2) transformation rotation = STANDARD RIGHT-HANDED in WORLD coords on all three axes ([0,90,0]: (-4,-4,-4)->(-4,-4,+4); [90,0,0] -> top/north; [0,0,90] -> east/bottom). (3) ORDER: X first, then Y, then Z (v' = Rz Ry Rx v): [90,90,0] -> (-4,+4,+4) and [90,0,90] -> (-4,-4,-4) fit only this order; [180,90,0] -> (+4,+4,+4) agrees.
- CONSEQUENCE (L-CAL-1 class, my tool): civ_render.py applied the transformation with the BONE law in file space (world-equivalent Rz(rz) Ry(-ry) Rx(-rx)) -> every E/W-facing piece drawn mirrored (east<->west) in ROOF-KIT.png and every civ_render sheet; X sign wrong too (only matters for non-180 X). N/S pieces and 180-flips unaffected. Fixing the renderer BEFORE judging any roof piece.
- Lesson candidate L-XFORM-LAW: minecraft:transformation rotates in WORLD space, right-handed, X->Y->Z, about the block centre; bone/cube rotations follow the separate file-space bone law (D-C255). Tools must not share one transform for both.

## D-C507 — THE FAILSAFE + the recoverable-delete guard (his 02:16 / 02:18 / 02:21 / 02:22 10-03) and the incident it caught (02:20–02:29 CT 10-03)
- HIS RULINGS (verbatim intent): stopping points to stop / verify / disconnect / restart; the garbage folder is the recoverable delete; clear the sandbox into his Drive when necessary with instant recovery; a folder I can DUMP into but never DELETE from — a failsafe holding every current, correct detail and file for the aftermath of a failure on either side; he uploads everything correct and current to Drive occasionally and gives me the same space. Then (02:27): continue the week's review for 6 hours or until done, hold all questions, he runs the CIVITAS trial + "p?? to p??" on return (= p22 + p23); (02:28) the 3-minute update interval stays.
- BUILT: tools/pw_safe.py (loaded into every python process by ~/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/usercustomize.py): shutil.rmtree / os.remove / os.unlink / Path.unlink inside /home/claude become MOVES into _garbage/<stamp>/<rel> (logged in _logs/pw_safe_ledger.md); real deletes only outside the workspace, in dot-dirs, inside _garbage (how the Drive archiver frees space) or with PW_ALLOW_DELETE=1. /root/.local/bin/rm + mv shims do the same for the shell. _failsafe/ is APPEND-ONLY: delete, unlink, rmtree, rmdir, rename, move-out all raise FailsafeError (PW_ALLOW_DELETE included); the shims refuse. Self-test 10/10.
- INCIDENT (caught, recovered, fixed): at 02:20 the first guard build resolved the ENTRY NAMES that shutil.rmtree's internals pass with dir_fd against the CWD and moved the real /home/claude/_bds into _garbage while the Drive archiver removed a verified folder (a plain delete would have failed harmlessly; the guard turned it into a move of the wrong tree). Recovered in one mv (the harness, logs and pristine world intact). FIX: dir_fd calls are never guarded; rmdir keeps its original semantics (an empty dir has nothing to recover); remove/unlink only ever move FILES; regression test = rmtree of a garbage archive whose entry names also exist in the CWD. LESSON CANDIDATE: a safety wrapper must preserve the original call's failure modes — a call that would have FAILED must not be turned into one that succeeds on a different target.
- tools/failsafe.py: `snapshot NOTE` streams a md5-verified failsafe-<stamp>.tar of the RECORD (_logs, _docs, tools, root *.md, every _build manifest + PW-DEPENDENCIES, the gofile folder records; no secrets; bulk images / >4 MiB dumps / garbage manifests left out and LISTED in the README) to Drive "AR-Failsafe" with its manifest + a README that says how to restore from Drive alone (restore = the streamed, md5-checked member pull); local record _failsafe/<stamp>/ (README, manifest, ENTRY) + INDEX.md appended. `builds NAME…` uploads each frozen build dir ONCE to AR-Failsafe/builds (ledger-guarded; never re-uploaded, never removed locally). New files only — the tool has no update or delete call.
- DISK: 97 % (1.4 GB free) — 86 world copies in _garbage (one per server run); archive job running for 85 of them (the quarantine-apk folder is never archived). The archiver's own rmtree inside _garbage runs the original path (regression-tested).
- ASSUMPTIONS for the 6-hour window: fixes for DEFECTS proven in the server ship without asking (as 210 did); anything that is a RULING (densities, vanilla biomes, swamp oaks, daughter distance) is held and listed. Reports every 3 minutes (his 02:28), snapshots at every stopping point.

## D-C509 — THE BRIDGE PAIR: a deck re-laid as a road because its own planks count as ground; gravel falls (03:07 CT 10-03; lay log civtest-20261003-025946)
- INSTRUMENT: bp02-211-laylog (job-only) logged every write to the watched cells; evoprobe-0.0.20 printed it. (189,346): seq 1 BRIDGE by key (189,345) w1 (g 66, drop 4 → planks at 70); seq 6 NORMAL by the jog key (190,346) w0 with g = 70 (groundAt walked onto the fresh planks: not in NOT_GROUND) → drop 0 → `top.setType(grass_path)` turned the deck plank into a path over the gully; seq 11 hardening → gravel; gravel FELL to 67 (the bridge lay had cleared 67–69). Twin (190,346) identical. (191,346) (w2 of the jog) got a proper bridge lay and keeps its planks. (189,347): normal fill at seq 2 then re-topped at seq 9 — stays (dirt under it). (26,74) granddaughter: normal lay with g 91 > h 90 (a 1-deep cut) over a HOLLOW (air at 88–89) → path at 90 → gravel → fell to 88.
- ROOT: layPlannedStreet trusted groundAt (topmost non-plant block) and never checked the support under a surface; our own surfaces (planks, path) count as ground, so an overlapping shape (a jog cross over a run body) re-laid a deck as a normal cell.
- FIX (tools/bp02_src/pw_civ_clock.js → bp02-211 rebuilt): (a) a cell already carrying a STREET_SURFACE (path / gravel / cobble / spruce planks) at h is left alone (`laid++`); (b) supportUnder(dim, x, h, z): after every normal street lay and every yard cell, air / water / plants under the surface are filled with dirt down to the first solid block (max 6). Lay test 169/169. Regression: evo 0.0.19 on the rebuilt 211 (expect bad 0) + inspect of the bridge (planks at 70 on both cells).
- LESSON CANDIDATES: (1) "ground" must exclude what we ourselves lay — a second pass over our own blocks must see them as ours, not as terrain; (2) a placed surface block needs support: gravel and sand fall, and a path over a cave roof is a path over nothing; (3) the per-cell lay log beats stack-reading for "who wrote this".
- RETRO-SWEEP (qualifying: confirmed defect + lesson): CIVITAS — HIT: paveSquare / terrace / stoop / docks place surfaces too — audit each for the support rule (S, P2) · HIT: groundAt callers that run after our own lays (yardPass hereH, settle(), buildWall, quarry) read our surfaces as ground — right for most (a yard on a street level), wrong when the surface is a deck (M, P3, investigate) · build tooling — HIT: the lay log instrument becomes a standing probe option (S) · worldgen — NO-HIT · trees — NO-HIT · others NO-HIT.

## D-C513 — TREES ON SNOW: the hypothesis chain, the measurements, and why 1.3.213 is HELD (04:11 CT 10-03)
- MEASURED (census 0.0.4, 197 land chunks, 6 biomes, bp02-212): our trees per chunk by snow cover <25 % 0.80 · 25–74 % 0.05 · ≥75 % 0.00 (the grove: all 6 of ours in its 8 bare chunks, 0 in 25 snowy ones).
- v1 (search_feature y then y−1, snow_layer already allowed): ≥75 % still 0; bare 0.80 → 1.11 (the second try beats plant-covered columns). v2 (grounded → leveled, solid-only intersection): bare 1.99 but FLOATING (under-root histogram: forest 58/115 on AIR, snowy taiga 10 on WATER) and ≥75 % still 0 → grounded is the anti-float guard, not the snow blocker. REJECTED, discarded.
- MARKER PROBE (snowprobe-0.0.1 + census 0.0.6): single-block markers DO place in the snow chunks (grove 51 + 47 in 13 chunks); the surface there is FULL SNOW BLOCKS (minecraft:snow: 1 deep over dirt in the grove, 2 deep on snowy slopes) — never in the allowlist, and not "ground" for grounded.
- v3 (grounded kept, snow + powder_snow allowed, solid-only intersection, search y−2..y): under-root CLEAN (grass / dirt / podzol only), bare 1.40/chunk (+75 % vs 212 — the slope fix lets templates place where their empty cells used to collide with hillsides), ≥75 % snow STILL 0. Relief census inconclusive (the surface sample reads canopies as relief).
- REMAINING HYPOTHESIS: steepness — snow lies on the high, steep chunks where a 7–13-wide template's solid canopy cuts into the mountainside (not allowed) while 1-block markers place freely; vanilla's trees are grown procedurally and adapt. TEST NEXT: a GROUND relief measure (ignore leaves / logs) per chunk; LEVERS: adjustment_radius 3–4 (the template slides to a valid spot), smaller templates in mountain biomes, or a mountain rule that places only young templates.
- HELD: bp02-213 v3 is sound on its own terms (no floating, snow blocks allowed) but raises bare-ground density 0.80 → 1.40 — that touches his densities ASSUMPTION → NOT shipped; 212 stays. Question 6 for him: take the +75 % (closer to Java's 8 per chunk), scale the rules back (fewer iterations), or hold.
- LESSONS: (1) a fix is proven by its census, not by its reasoning — v1 and v2 each sounded right and both failed; (2) the under-root histogram is a standing gate for any placement change (floating never again); (3) a single-block marker separates "the rule fires" from "the feature fits"; (4) the official Features.html (bedrock-samples/documentation) is on disk now — read the constraint semantics before the next attempt.
- RETRO-SWEEP (qualifying: lesson + tooling): trees — HIT: ground-relief census + adjustment_radius experiment (M, held with Q6) · build tooling — HIT: biomecensus 0.0.4–0.0.7 = a per-chunk census family; fold into one tool with flags (S) · documentation — HIT: FOUNDATION lesson "snow biomes' surface is full snow blocks" (S). NO-HIT: CIVITAS, terrain, redwood, mobs, atmospherics, PBR, blocks, scripts, audio.

The residual blocker on full-snow-block terrain is unexplained after v3 (snow blocks allowed, grounded on dirt beneath, solid-only intersection, search y−2..y). Candidates left for a fresh session: `grounded`'s notion of ground vs the block under the structure ORIGIN rather than the root; `unburied` on sloped snow; the pool's 13-wide templates vs mountain stone at canopy height. The measurement harness (biomecensus 0.0.4–0.0.8 + snowprobe) is ready; the next experiment should be a single young template (7 wide) placed by a dedicated rule at adjustment_radius 4 in the grove, counted by the census.

## D-C515 — DEFECT PROVEN by the two-run probe: our light blocks are never removed (flattened ids) — and the persistence results (06:04 CT 10-03)
- PERSISTENCE (A civtest-20261003-055700 → B -055954 on the DELIVERED 212 → C -060052): HEARTH LEDGER PROVEN — "ledger loaded: 2 hearth(s)" (H3's drop persisted), H1 lit / H2 fueled / H3 stone after the restart; the absolute clock persisted (A 728 → B 817); a jump to 6398 turned H1 to embers at 6628 = litUntil 6598 + 30 (inside one 40-tick cycle); after B the stored H1 read spent with emberUntil 18598 = 6598 + 2 x 6000 (embers = twice the lit time, as ruled). onPlace registers a hearth placed by /setblock (no player). WEATHER CACHE PROVEN ({"overworld":"Rain"} read raw before load after two restarts). SIDE MEASUREMENT: /time set day moves the absolute clock FORWARD to the next day (6628 → 25002, day 1); time add 24000 → 49004: no rewind, so our absolute-time timers never run backwards.
- THE DEFECT: pw_mob_light.clearLight (1.3.194, 09-30) and the golden-crown aura's _pwClearCrownLight (main.js, since 1.3.54) remove a light only when `typeId === "minecraft:light_block"`. On 1.26.52 the block that `BlockPermutation.resolve("minecraft:light_block", {block_light_level: N})` places reads `minecraft:light_block_N` (Bedrock flattened the light block into 16 ids; run A: light_block_13 in air, light_block_6 waterlogged). So clearLight returns "cleared" WITHOUT touching the block and the record is dropped. ## D-C541 [22:28 CT 10-03] HIS 22:28 — NO IDLE VILLAGERS, NO "MANIFESTED" TOWNS: EVERY EXPANSION IS BUILT FROM REAL RESOURCES, POPULATION AND MONEY
- RULING (his words, paraphrased): villagers are never "doing nothing" — purpose in their movements, their purchases, their collecting of materials for tomorrow's build; they mine and BREAK BLOCKS and STORE them. Villages/towns/cities do not "manifest": they come from the settlement's ability to create them from its resources and population. On an upgrade or expansion the right amount of resources is DOCKED, money MOVES, people get NEW JOBS and HOMES — an ACTUAL expansion, not magic.
- WHAT ALREADY HOLDS (economy v2): a stage's bill of materials is read from the template's block counts and must be in stock before the stage is placed; wages move pennies treasury -> purse -> tills; the quarry's output is the blocks really dug from a growing pit; the people model hires into vacancies and moves people into homes with room. WHAT IS STILL "MAGIC": embodied villagers stand in their shops instead of walking to work; stone leaves the pit without a worker swinging at it; stock lives only in the ledger (no chest fills); builders are not seen at the site; the tier-up itself has no visible act.

- Research tie-in: R2 (wages / BOM) stands; R5 adds the medieval work day (dawn to dusk, Sunday rest) for C2.1.

## D-C546 [23:35 CT 10-03] HIS 23:35 — THE STEPPED TOWN: parallel streets as storeys, switchbacks along the MAIN road to climb, parcels along it; northeast-US hill cities (stairs between buildings and in alleys) as the model
- RULING (his words, paraphrased): parallel streets allow a storied / stepped town: switchbacks along the main road climb in elevation while strips of business/building parcels line both sides of the main roads through town. Investigate how northeast-United-States cities developed this (they use STAIRS to climb between buildings and in alleys); in his opinion these are the most interesting city layouts.
- REFINES C5 (23:3x reading): the bare 7-wide switchback roads stay for reaching benches; the TOWN'S OWN main road may switchback up a hill with parcels on its legs.
- GEOMETRY (the engine's constraint, stated for him): a 13-wide axis-aligned kit street climbs 1 in 7, so on a 28 % hillside it can only run ALONG the contour (level) — any climb would put it 17 blocks into or above the ground within one block length. Therefore the stepped town = TERRACE STREETS (13-wide, along the contour, one per storey, ~60 apart = ~17 blocks of height on a 28 % slope) joined by (a) NARROW CLIMBING LEGS: his 7-wide road at 1 in 4 running straight up the fall line between two tee windows (47 cells climb 12, which is about the ground's own fall there), the hairpin at alternating ends of the terraces = the "switchback along the main road"; (b) STAIR ALLEYS: 3-wide pedestrian stairs between plots mid-block (the Pittsburgh / Cincinnati city steps), one per ~26 cells of block; (c) parcels on both sides of every terrace street: the uphill row cut into the hill (cellar in the slope, 3 < cut <= 6 stepped), the downhill row on podiums / stilts (3 < fill <= 12).
- BUILD (phase B3, after B's caps): openKitSideStreet on a hill: when the parallel's level differs from the base's by more than the 13-wide connector can climb (> 6 over 47 cells), plan the parallel at ITS OWN ground level and join it with a narrow 1-in-4 road (planRoadJob between the two windows) instead of a kit connector; stair alleys as a new op ("stair": stone-brick stairs 3 wide with landings every 6 risers, hand-rails of fences); the main street at founding prefers the contour direction on a hill (relief > 6 across the candidates); the wall ring follows the terraces.
- RESEARCH (R5 brief extended): Pittsburgh's city steps (700+ public stairways), Cincinnati's hillside steps (~400), Providence's College Hill, Boston's Beacon Hill, Troy / Albany / Yonkers / Manayunk, the New England mill-town section (mill on the river, housing rows up the slope: Lowell, Manchester NH, Paterson), Duluth as the extreme case: street spacing by elevation, stair lengths, parcel depths, how business strips sat on the switchback legs.

## D-C547 [23:55 CT 10-03] HIS 23:55 — "sewers within our roads need logic to find their appropriate EXIT POINTS" (additions keep coming; all are additions to the current work)
- TODAY: every kit dead end gets its own outfall — a tunnel to the nearest daylight lower than the trench floor (planOutfall; exits verified against live blocks, a grate, water spilling) — regardless of where the water in that street actually runs, and with no notion of a river or of one network draining to one place.
- DESIGN (A0.2 "sewer exits v2", added to the work table): (1) the DRAINAGE GRAPH per settlement: the trench cells of every piece, joined through tees / crossroads / connectors; the floor height of each cell from the street's profile (ramps step the trench); (2) the network's LOW POINTS (local minima of the floor along the streets) are where water collects — the exits are chosen there, not at every end; (3) an exit's TARGET: the best of (a) open water (river / lake / sea) within 120 blocks whose surface is below the floor, (b) a daylight slope face lower than the floor (today's rule), (c) a dry well / soakaway shaft dug 8 below the trench when the land is flat and dry (the medieval cesspit) — ranked water > face > soakaway, nearest first; (4) one trunk per network minimum, the other dead ends SEALED (no grate, no tunnel), unless a second minimum cannot drain to the first; (5) the trunk's floor falls 1 per 7 toward the exit so the flow is real (a source block only at the network's high points and after each step; never a source wall), the outfall mouth lined, grated, and the spill cut as a channel to the water; (6) when a street grows or a cross street joins, the graph is re-solved and a now-redundant outfall is sealed (its tunnel back-filled); (7) the chronicle logs "the sewer of X drains to the river at …".
- Verification: the probe's sewerChecks extended with per-network exit counts, floor minima, and a dye test (a water pulse at the high point reaches the mouth).

## D-C548 [00:0x CT 10-04] CENSUS INTEGRATED (D-C536) — built, unverified; the ticking cores (D-C542) designed
- BUILT (patch_clock_219: census helpers): st.people = PEOPLE.newPeople() per settlement; a household's move-in records its people (names shared with the villagers at the door); every ledger day runs PEOPLE.dayStep (fed = yesterday's prosperity, paid = no arrears, homes with room = HOUSEHOLD x DENSITY minus the living, jobs = open shops' stations minus the people at them); weddings / births / deaths / inheritances / arrivals go to the chronicle and the player's events; st.mood = the mean mood; MOOD_GATE 45 on the tier-up; the notice board's first line = the freshest rumour; the status payload carries census {n, mood, married, children, rumours, threads} (the census itself stays out of the 2 KB message). population() still counts dwellings (hands vs census: C2 decides).

## D-C549 [00:03 CT 10-04] HIS 00:03 — SUBSTRUCTURES MAY RUN BEYOND THE STREETS TO DRAIN; CITY WORKS = THE ENGINE OF ADVANCEMENT; BORDERS GROW ONLY WHEN A VILLAGER MOVES THE BOUNDARY STONES
- RULING 1 (his words, paraphrased): a sewer may continue UNDERGROUND where no road, street or path lies above it IF that creates an exit point required by the natural flow of water (which the sewers now have) and the need to drain somewhere. The city-planning modules AND TESTS must include the substructures: roads and the substructures he designed beneath them are the beginning of real human civilization ADVANCEMENT — civilizations rose and fell repeatedly before roads, gutters, sanitation (sewers, waste removal, plumbing, hospitals) and other city works became normal, so these works are a large part of why our civs expand.
- RULING 2: REGULAR BORDER GROWTH with checks; villagers must go out and MOVE the placement rocks marking the edge of their settlement's influence as it grows — the border never just "grows": the border blocks are moved by a villager BEFORE the influence expands. This opens conflict over land, negotiation, and conflict resolution or escalation.
- DESIGN (ASSUMPTIONS for witness): (A0.2 extended) trunk sewers run underground beyond the streets to the chosen exit (D-C547's water > face > soakaway targets), lined, with manholes where they pass under open ground every 26 cells (F3), the probe's sewerChecks extended to the whole drainage graph (trunks included) + the dye test. (F7 CIVIC WORKS LADDER, new) each tier requires its works before it can rise, built like any plot from the ledger: village: well + sewer trench; village III: gutters on every street + a midden cart post (waste removal job); town I: public latrine + a water cistern; town III: a bathhouse + the lamplighter post; city I: an aqueduct or well-house feeding the cistern + an INFIRMARY (the first hospital) + the sewer trunks sealed/grated; city III: a hospital proper + public fountains; metropolis: water towers, hospital wards per neighbourhood. The census gets a SANITATION dial (works present vs people): low sanitation lowers mood and raises deaths (sickness as nature, not crime — Utopia-First stands); the chronicle names the works ("the bathhouse opened; the town is cleaner").
- (B4 BORDER STONES, new) the influence border is a ring of boundary stones (a `pw:border_stone` cairn every 16 cells on the ring) placed by a SURVEYOR (the reeve's post from village II). Growth of influence = the surveyor walks to each stone and carries it outward (an embodied task: pick up, walk, place); only when the whole ring stands at the new radius does the influence (plot search, benches, quarry pits, wood stands) extend. Where another settlement's ring is met the stone cannot be moved: a DISPUTE thread opens between the two councils (the people model's threads: default course = a shared boundary after 20 days; other courses: a land purchase (money moves between ledgers), a concession for representation rights, or ESCALATION — an embargo (trade stops) and border patrols; no violence until he rules on it). The chronicle and both notice boards carry the dispute.

## D-C550 [00:43 / 00:52 CT 10-04] HIS 00:43 + 00:52 — VILLAGERS THAT LEARN: a condensed "seek more / question yourself" drive; experience + time + learning factor; trust and opinions from experience; "am I too ambitious?"; implementation left to me; goal-driven purpose under the real-materials rule
- RULING (his words, paraphrased): villagers get an extremely condensed version of the logic that drives Claude to seek other sources — a knowledge of the need to do more and to seek it out; the mark of human thought is the ability to question itself; learn, remember and grow from experiences (experience + time + learning factor, or a derivative Claude manufactures) so a villager learns from experience, trusts someone more or less from it, and develops opinions. Not a thinking module per villager — growth. City growth and structure placement must be MORE than "intuitive", and under the actual-use-of-materials rule the villagers need enough logic and constant purpose to be goal-driven "intuitively". He leaves the how to Claude.
- ANSWER GIVEN: not too ambitious as a design; ambitious as an engine problem only if cognition is per-tick thinking — it is not: a LEARNING RULE on a few numbers per record and per relationship, updated by events, is both the condensed version of "seeking" and cheap. Order matters more than ambition: the literal material loop (C2) first, because the learning layer feeds on its events.
- DESIGN (D-C550 = the behaviour layer of C2; ASSUMPTIONS for witness):
  (1) MEMORY per person (the census record): trust per other person / shop / place / source (0..1, starts 0.5); opinions per topic (the council, the quarry, the road to X, the player, a partner town) as the same number; expectation per routine (how long the trip to the pit takes, how much the bakery had).
  (2) THE LEARNING RULE (experience + time + learning factor): after every outcome o in [0,1]: v <- v + a * (o - v), with a = 1 / (n + 2) (the n-th experience: fast at first, settling later — the learning factor), and a drift toward neutral 0.5 of b = 0.01 per day without contact (time — forgetting). Surprise = |o - v| is the SELF-QUESTIONING signal: a big surprise raises the person's exploration e (below) and makes a rumour ("the baker was out of bread again").
  (3) THE DRIVE (needs -> goals -> acts): every embodied villager keeps a small pressure vector (hunger, shelter/rest, work/pay, materials for tomorrow's build, company, curiosity) rising with time and falling when met; each beat it takes the highest-pressure goal and the act with the best EXPECTED value (trust-weighted), with an exploration share e (10 % base, up after surprises) spent on an untried source — the "need to do more and seek it out". Outcomes feed rule (2). A failed act lowers trust in that source (the shop was empty, the road was blocked) and the next choice differs.
  (4) OPINIONS -> BEHAVIOUR: buyer choice = price x distance x standing x fondness x trust (the canon's formula gains trust); who they tell rumours to (friends with high trust), who they vote for at the council, whether they join a caravan, whether they move away (low trust in the town), how they treat the player (greetings by trust + fondness).
  (5) GROWTH of the PERSON: skills per trade rise with days worked (output per swing/bake rises 1 % per 10 days to a cap), apprentices learn from a master in the same shop (a journeyman at 20 days, a master at 200), masters teach faster; the chronicle records the first master in each trade.
  (6) GROWTH of the TOWN from the same signals: a shop with low trust everywhere closes; a route everyone avoids is repaired first; a council (town I+) chooses the next civic work by the loudest unmet pressure (hunger -> a second bakery, materials -> a second quarry, company -> a square or inn) — the planning becomes goal-driven, not a fixed TIER_ADDS list (the list stays as the fallback order).
  (7) COST: numbers in records, event-driven; nothing per tick but the embodied hands' goal pick (a few comparisons each). Verified in the node tests (test_people) before the server.

## D-C565 (19:1x CT 10-04) — the Phase-6 fall-direction sign closed BY LAW (not by the pending witness datum)
- Derivation: the fall animation turns the root bone by a NEGATIVE z rotation; L-ROT-DIR (D-C255, verified against vanilla bind
  poses + witnessed) says +rz tips the top toward file +x, so the trunk tips toward file -x = the entity's RIGHT. A Bedrock
  entity at yaw psi faces (-sin psi, cos psi); its right is (-cos psi, -sin psi). The script's convention (-cos psi, +sin psi)
  was a reflection across the x axis — exactly July's witness ("2x2 fell dead-opposite; elders a quarter turn off").
- Built: pw_fall_physics.fallDirOfYaw / yawOfFallDir with FALL_Z_SIGN = -1; every yaw<->direction site in main.js goes through
  them (forced 2x2 yaw, the 8-direction picker, the sweep, the pin, the particles, the drops). +1 restores the old convention.
- Status: law-derived, NOT witnessed (P1). His one fell + the [FELL] line's compass word decide; if the trunk lies opposite the
  printed direction the sign flips in one place.

## D-C1006-DYN (his 21:39 / 21:47 CT) — QUEUED program after 228: households, homes and dynasty
- Grown children move out at adulthood whenever a home is free (not only from an overfull home), linked to the parents only through a DYNASTY record; once out they marry and have children.
- Moving out = an UPGRADE: the new household takes a better home when one is free.
- After the parents die the heir SELLS the old home (or moves into it if it is better); sale proceeds go to the heir.
- HIS RULE: when someone moves OUT of and/or INTO a home, the home is RESTORED from its weathered state to fresh (EN2 weathering reset) — a job for builders, money spent; home SALES replenish those costs. This keeps cities updated naturally.
- Ties to the population goal (5,000–10,000 eventually) and the measured founder die-off (~day 170-200).
